text: Books are a uniquely portable magic. They can transport us to other worlds, introduce us to people we'll never meet, and teach us lessons we didn't know we needed.

title: Why I stopped forcing myself to finish bad books
text: Life is too short and the TBR pile is too high. I used to feel guilty abandoning a book halfway through, but now I see it as an act of self-respect. There are too many wonderful stories waiting for me to waste time on one that doesn't spark joy...

title: There's something about re-reading a favorite book
text: The first read is about discovery. The second read is about understanding. The third? It's like coming home. You notice the little things you missed before — a line of dialogue, a subtle foreshadowing, the way the author builds tension. Re-reading is an act of love, both for the book and for the person you were when you first read it.
I have always imagined that Paradise will be a kind of library.

title: The movie is almost never better than the book
text: There, I said it. Movies can capture plot and dialogue, but they can never capture the intimacy of being inside a character's head. The way a book lets you hear someone's unspoken thoughts, feel their emotions from the inside — that's magic no screen can replicate. That said, I'll still watch every adaptation and complain about what they changed.

title: On reading slowly in a fast world
text: We're told to optimize everything, to read more books faster, to hit our Goodreads goal. But some books deserve to be savored like a fine tea. I've started letting myself linger over beautiful sentences, re-read paragraphs that make me catch my breath, and close the book to stare out the window and think. Reading isn't a race. It's a journey.
